name: Yandjibara
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog yand1261 lists only Breen 1990 subclassification comment; no descriptive material found for Yandjibara

sources.citation: Breen, Gavan. 1990. Salvage studies of western Queensland Aboriginal languages. Pacific Linguistics B-105. Canberra: ANU. Chapter 4 'The languages of the Upper Barcoo', pp. 65-107; sec. 4.3(b) 'Yandjibara' phonology pp. 70-72 (PDF pp. 82-84), Table 4.3 p. 72.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.3(b) is a phoneme-inventory reconstruction from the three Curr wordlists (loss of initial velar stop, /rd/ vs /r/, possible trill and retroflex nasal, no final consonants) and says only that Yandjibara 'is probably basically similar to Bidjara' (p. 70). The word 'stress' occurs in the volume only for Kungkari (sec. 3.2.2 p. 26: 'Main stress is on the first vowel of a word'), Guwa (p. 118, Roth's italics) and Yanda (p. 147) — different languages.

sources.note: Not a Yandjibara source, but Breen 1990:70 models Yandjibara phonology on Bidjara ('probably basically similar to Bidjara'); Breen 1973 is the primary stress statement for the closest described relative (Bidyara, bidy1243) and is the only conceivable proxy. Would be an analogical inference, not a Yandjibara statement.
